# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Keep every `> **System**` panel from the mastered chapter, including a notice the narrator only hears. Do not turn a panel into italics, a sound effect, or narration. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks. Keep a mastered thought in italics. Do not turn it into spoken dialogue.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

＃223화



전율.

전투를 지켜본 모두가 느낀 감정이다.

진태경의 실력이 뛰어나다는 것은 진작 알고 있었다. 지금까지 봐 온 것이 그의 전부가 아니라는 것도.

‘하지만 이 정도였다니.’

최 팀장, 아니 최민우는 마른침을 삼켰다.

그는 비록 긴 시간은 아니지만 지난 몇 달간 진태경을 가장 가까이서 지켜본 사람이다.

그러나 이 순간, 최민우는 진태경에 관한 자신의 판단이 모두 틀렸음을 깨달았다.

‘이 사람은…… 도대체 뭐지?’

지금까지의 모든 것들은 빙산의 일각에 불과했다.

헌터 인력 사무소에서 처음 만난 몇 개월 전. 일당 수십만 원에 짐꾼을 자처하던 그가, 홀로 네임드 몬스터를 사냥했다.

그것도 압도적으로.

푸욱-!

오러를 머금은 창날이 미간을 꿰뚫는다.

그토록 강대하던 네임드 몬스터가 단 한 사람에 의해 죽은 순간이었고, 새로운 전설이 탄생하는 순간이기도 했다.

“도련님.”

“……아.”

잠시 넋을 놓고 있던 최민우는 김 집사의 부름에 겨우 정신을 차릴 수 있었다.

주위를 둘러보니 모두가 비슷한 표정이었다.

경악. 그리고 경악. 알 수 없는 전율에 몸을 떨던 그들은 약속이라도 한 것처럼 진태경을 향해 달려 나갔다.

“진태경 씨!”

“태경아!”

그들을 향해 진태경이 웃는다. 일말의 후회조차 털어 버린 듯한 후련한 미소에 최민우는 헛웃음이 나왔다.

“지금 웃음이 나옵니까?”

“글쎄요. 딱히 뭘 할지 모르겠어서.”

“차라리 소리를 지르십시오. 어차피 우리밖에 없는데.”

“내가 네임드 몬스터를 죽였다! 뭐 이렇게요?”

“네, 이제야 좀 실감이 나네요.”

뒤통수를 긁적이는 진태경을 물끄러미 바라보던 최민우가 불쑥 손을 내밀었다.

잠깐 잊고 있던 한마디가 떠올랐기 때문이었다.

만약, 아주 만약에 그가 승리한다면 꼭 해 주고 싶었던 말이 있었다.

“고생하셨습니다.”

“…….”

“지금까지 정말 고생 많으셨어요.”

순간 진태경의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다.

맑고 깊은 검은 눈동자에 형용할 수 없는 감정이 스친 것도 잠시, 그는 굳게 손을 맞잡았다.

“고맙습니다. 다른 분들도 모두요.”



* * *



나는 사방에서 날아드는 질문과 축하 세례에 한동안 정신을 차리지 못했다.

“그게 벌써 30년 전이군요. 한창 대격변이 진행되고 있던 때였는데…….”

“아, 예.”

평소 감정 표현이 드문 김 집사는 흥분된 목소리로 대격변 당시 있었던 사건들을 나열했으며.

“세상에. 이거 꿈 아니죠? 아니, 아니지?”

“어, 아냐.”

송송이는 여전히 이게 꿈인지 생시인지 분간이 안 된다는 얼굴로 나를 바라봤고.

“크흑. 태경아! 이 자식아! 크흐흐흑!”

“……아니, 아저씨는 왜 또 울어요?”

“기특해서 그래. 인마. 기특해서. 크흐흡!”

임꺽정은 마치 친자식이 살아 돌아온 것처럼 울음을 터트렸다.

이런 상황이니 잔뜩 밀려 있는 시스템 메시지를 확인할 겨를도 없었다.

결국 혼란스러운 상황을 정리한 것은 최 팀장이었다.

“자자, 다들 진정하시고 뒤처리부터 하시죠.”

“그, 좋은 의견이긴 한데요.”

나는 조심스럽게 가장 중요한 물음을 던졌다.

“뒤처리를 어떻게 하죠?”

“……어. 그게 그러니까.”

늘 모든 일에 막힘이 없던 최 팀장도 당황한 기색이 역력했다.

레이드 후 뒤처리는 항상 해 왔던 일이고 늘 비슷하다.

사상자를 확인, 치료하는 것과 부산물을 정리해서 챙기는 것. 여기에 굳이 덧붙이자면 장비를 점검하는 것 정도다.

하지만 이번에는 경우가 달랐다.

‘이놈 몸통 길이만 50m가 넘는데.’

이건 어디까지나 길이만 따졌을 때 이야기고, 엄청난 굵기에 날개, 꼬리 등등은 별개의 문제다.

이걸 어떻게 처리할지 생각하는 것만으로도 머리가 아파 왔다.

‘그렇다고 이걸 버리고 갈 수도 없고.’

부산물 처리는 가죽과 뼈, 살까지 분리해 내야 하는 작업이다.

내가 쓰러트린 카루스는 무려 네임드 몬스터씩이나 되는 놈이다 보니 그 희소성과 난이도는 상상을 초월했다.

‘시벌, 비늘은 또 어떻게 하냐.’

식칼로 슥슥 긁어 낼 수 있는 생선 비늘 따위가 아니다.

나를 제외하면 김 집사, 최 팀장 정도쯤은 되어야 가능한 작업 난이도. 물론 방법이 없는 것은 아니었다.

딱 하나, 아주 쉬우면서 동시에 어려운 방법이 남아 있긴 하지.

‘인벤토리.’

지금껏 경험한 바에 의하면 인벤토리의 수용량은 거의 무한대에 가깝다. 게다가 살아 있는 생명체도 아닌 몬스터의 사체. 충분히 시도해 볼 만했다.

‘문제는 그다음이지.’

인벤토리에 카루스의 사체를 집어넣으면 사람들이 무슨 반응을 보일지 눈에 선하다.

만에 하나 길드원들에게는 솔직하게 털어놓는다고 쳐도, 부산물을 평생 간직하지 않는 이상 의혹이 생길 것이다.

‘게이트 입구에서 기자들이 진을 치고 있는데 대체 어떻게 몰래 갖고 나왔냐, 등등.’

그렇게 된다면 얼마 지나지 않아 전 국민이 내 비밀을 알게 될지도 모른다.

일간신문 1면과 뉴스 헤드라인은 내 이름으로 장식되겠지.



[충격 속보) A급 헌터 진태경, 시스템 사용자로 밝혀져.]

[진태경과의 인터뷰. “무공이 제일 쉬웠어요.”]

[헌터 협회, “진태경의 헌터 자격증 박탈해야.”]

[진태경, 헌터 협회를 향한 일갈, “시벌, 꼬우면 니들도 시스템 쓰든가.”]

[NASA 공식 입장, “반드시 그를 잡아 실험대에 올려놓을 것.”]



“…….”

“진태경 씨? 왜 그러십니까?”

“아뇨. 그냥 생각만으로도 아찔해서.”

“예?”

“그런 게 있습니다.”

절대로 있어서는 안 되는 일이지. 아무렴.

결국, 모두가 머리를 맞대고 고민한 끝에 한 가지 의견이 최종적으로 채택되었다.

최 팀장이 판관처럼 엄숙한 목소리로 선언했다.

“외부 인력 끌어옵시다.”

게이트는 상록수처럼 변함없는 공간이 아니다.

일정 시간이 지나면 파괴된 환경과 몬스터가 복구되는데, 이 현상을 리젠(Regen)이라 부르며 게이트의 등급에 따라 리젠까지 걸리는 시간도 달랐다.

“제가 알기로 A급 게이트는 통상 일주일에 한 번씩 리젠됩니다. 오늘이 1일 차니까 시간은 충분해요.”

최대한 빠르게 외부 인력을 끌어와 진행 속도를 높이자는 것. 지금으로서는 가장 타당하고 실현 가능성이 높은 의견이었다.

다만, 이 계획에도 약간의 애로사항은 있었다.

“출구 게이트가 안 열렸는데요.”

말 그대로였다.

네임드 몬스터를 때려잡았으니 응당 출구가 열려야 하는데, 어찌 된 일인지 수십 분이 흐른 지금까지도 묵묵부답이다.

임꺽정도 불안한 얼굴로 주위를 둘러봤다.

“그러게. 이거 왜 안 열려? 혹시 게이트가 고장 난 건가?”

“…….”

끔찍한 소리 하네.

로그인 무림으로도 모자라서 로그인 게이트. 뭐 그런 거라면 차라리 혀 깨물고 죽는 게 낫겠다.

영 쎄한 기분을 느끼고 있을 때, 김 집사가 입을 열었다.

“보스 몬스터가 살아 있는 모양입니다.”

“살아 있다고요? 보스 몬스터가?”

내가 피 웅덩이에 고개를 박고 쓰러져 있는 카루스의 사체를 가리키자 김 집사가 고개를 가로저었다.

“네임드 몬스터와 보스 몬스터는 다릅니다. 간단하게 설명해 드리자면…… 전자는 불청객, 후자는 본래 있던 집주인이라고 해야 맞겠죠.”

“I’d beat him until he begged me to kill him.”

The inside of a Gate was ultimately a world ruled by the law of the jungle.

The strong reigned, and the weak were trampled.

From the boss monster’s perspective, running away had been a fairly wise decision.

*Unfortunately, that just made things more troublesome for us.*

There was no way the thing had fled for its life only to hang around nearby grooming its claws.

It would have hidden as far away and as secretly as possible. And with only five people, searching this vast wasteland was impossible.

“Then…”

“We’ll have to go back to the entrance we came through.”

Team Leader Choi asked with concern in his eyes.

“You, Mr. Jin?”

*I just leveled up, damn it. Let me go.*

I swallowed the words that had risen to my throat and answered instead.

“I’m still full of energy. If you’re worried, I can have someone cast healing magic on me before I leave.”

“As you know, it’s a considerable distance to the entrance.”

“As you know, I’m pretty fast.”

It had taken us quite a while to reach this place the first time, but it would be different if I went alone. I wouldn’t have to stay on guard against monsters or match the pace of a group.

If I ran at full speed, I could reach the Gate entrance within an hour or two.

“Hmm. In that case, I’ll leave it to you. You and Butler Kim can go together.”

“Butler Kim, too?”

Butler Kim stroked his impressively full beard as he answered.

“We need to bring in outside personnel.”

Processing the byproducts of a Named Monster required Hunters who were at least B-Rank, if not A-Rank.

“I know a few people. If I go personally, they’ll probably drop everything and come running.”

That sounded about right.

*It was something I could hardly believe even after seeing it.*

Knowing Butler Kim’s spectacular track record, I could only nod. We needed him if we wanted to bring in outside personnel.

“So it’ll just be Butler Kim and me?”

“Yes.”

“All right. I’m ready.”

“Pardon?”

“Would you bend over a little?”

“……Why do you need me to bend over?”

No, what exactly was he ready for? Why did I need to bend over?

A terrible suspicion crossed my mind.

“You don’t mean…soap?”

“Please carry me on your back.”

“Oh. Sure.”

Thank goodness. He wasn’t a centaur.

I let out a sigh of relief and willingly offered my back to Butler Kim.

Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud!

With Butler Kim on my back, I raced forward without slowing down.

We ran into a pack of Orcs wandering through the wasteland, but that was the only interruption.

“Fire Rain.”

The magic of an A-Rank mage.

One-third of the Orcs died beneath the downpour of fire, and the rest scattered in every direction.

I felt like a mobile turret.

*This isn’t bad.*

Just as I was thinking about how much more efficient raids would be if I did them this way, we crossed the barren wasteland and spotted a dense jungle ahead.

“You’re astonishingly fast. We’ve already reached the jungle.”

“I’m going to slow down from here. With all this vegetation, we could get lost.”

“I’ll follow your lead, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”

“……Huh.”

Puzzled by my abrupt halt, Butler Kim asked,

“What is it?”

“It’s nothing. Just…”

How was I supposed to explain this?

At last, I found the right word and added softly,

“There are hyenas.”

“Hyenas?”

Stupid, persistent hyenas that kept baring their teeth even after I had let them go once.

I crooked my finger toward the dense undergrowth in the distance.

“Come out, you fucking bastards.”

Rustle.

The undergrowth shook, and the hyenas emerged one by one.

But my eyes were fixed on only one person.

> **System**
>
> **Lv. 80 Won Myunghoon**

“Would you look at this insolent bastard.”

The leader of the hyenas bared his teeth and growled.

Choi Minwoo let out a hollow laugh.

“You can smile at a time like this?”

“I don’t know. I can’t think of anything else to do.”

“Then shout, at least. We’re the only ones here anyway.”

“Something like, ‘I killed a Named Monster!’?”

“Yes. Now it’s finally starting to feel real.”

Choi Minwoo stared at Jin Taekyung as he scratched the back of his head, then abruptly held out his hand.

A sentence he had momentarily forgotten had come back to him.

Something he had wanted to say if—just if—Taekyung won.

“Thank you for all your hard work.”

“…….”

“You’ve truly been through so much.”

For an instant, Jin Taekyung’s eyelids trembled.

An indescribable emotion flickered through his clear, deep-black eyes. Then he firmly clasped Choi Minwoo’s hand.

“Thank you. All of you.”

* * *

For a while, I couldn’t come to my senses amid the barrage of questions and congratulations flying at me from every direction.

“So that was already thirty years ago. The Great Cataclysm was still in full swing at the time…”

“Ah, yes.”

Butler Kim, who rarely showed much emotion, excitedly rattled off one incident after another from the Great Cataclysm.

“My goodness. This isn’t a dream, is it? No, it isn’t, right?”

“Uh, no.”

Song Song stared at me as if she still couldn’t tell whether she was dreaming or awake.

“Sniff. Taekyung! You bastard! Sniff, sob!”

“……Why are you crying again, Uncle?”

“Because I’m proud of you, you punk. I’m proud. Sniff!”

Im Kkeokjeong burst into tears as if his own child had made it back alive.

With all that going on, I didn’t have a chance to check the backlog of System messages.

In the end, Team Leader Choi was the one who brought order to the chaos.

“All right, everyone, calm down. Let’s deal with the cleanup first.”

“That’s a good idea, but…”

I cautiously asked the most important question.

“How are we supposed to clean this up?”

“……Oh. Well, you see…”

Even Team Leader Choi, who was never at a loss in any situation, looked flustered.

Cleaning up after a raid was routine, and the work was generally the same every time.

Check and treat the casualties, then sort through and collect the byproducts. If there was anything else, it was usually just inspecting the Equipment.

But this time was different.

*This bastard’s torso alone is over fifty meters[^2] long.*

And that was only counting its length. Its enormous girth, wings, tail, and everything else were separate problems.

Just thinking about how to deal with it was giving me a headache.

*But we can’t just leave it here.*

Processing the byproducts meant separating the hide, bones, and flesh.

The Carus I had brought down was a Named Monster, so its rarity and the difficulty of processing it were beyond imagination.

*Fuck, what are we supposed to do with the scales?*

They weren’t fish scales we could scrape off with a kitchen knife.

Aside from me, someone would have to be at least as capable as Butler Kim or Team Leader Choi to handle the job. Of course, there was one possible solution.

There was one method left.

It was both extremely easy and extremely difficult.

*Inventory.*

Based on everything I had experienced so far, the Inventory’s capacity was practically infinite. Besides, this was a monster’s corpse, not a living creature.

It was worth a try.

*The problem comes afterward.*

I could already picture everyone’s reaction if I put Carus’s corpse into my Inventory.

Even if I came clean to the guild members, suspicions would arise unless I intended to keep the byproducts forever.

*Reporters are camped out at the Gate entrance, so how did he secretly carry all of it outside? Things like that.*

If that happened, it might not be long before the entire country learned my secret.

The front pages of the daily newspapers and every news headline would be decorated with my name.

> **Breaking News:** A-Rank Hunter Jin Taekyung Revealed to Be a System User

> **Interview with Jin Taekyung:** “Martial Arts Were the Easiest Part”

> **Hunter Association:** “Jin Taekyung’s Hunter License Must Be Revoked”

> **Jin Taekyung Blasts Hunter Association:** “Fuck, if You Don’t Like It, Use the System Yourselves”

> **NASA Official Statement:** “We Will Capture Him at All Costs and Subject Him to Experiments”

“…….”

“Mr. Jin Taekyung? Is something wrong?”

“No. Just thinking about it made me dizzy.”

“Pardon?”

“It’s nothing.”

That could never be allowed to happen. Absolutely not.

In the end, after everyone put their heads together, we settled on one solution.

Team Leader Choi announced the verdict with the solemnity of a judge.

“Let’s bring in outside personnel.”

Gates weren’t immutable spaces, unchanging as evergreen trees.

After a certain amount of time, their destroyed environments and monsters were restored. This phenomenon was called Regen, and the time it took for a Gate to undergo Regen varied according to its Grade.

“As far as I know, A-Rank Gates usually undergo Regen once a week. Today is only the first day, so we have plenty of time.”

We would bring in outside personnel as quickly as possible to speed up the work. For now, it was the most reasonable and feasible option.

There was, however, one small problem with the plan.

“The exit Gate hasn’t opened.”

That was exactly what had happened.

Now that we had beaten the Named Monster to death, the exit should have opened. Yet even after several dozen minutes, it still showed no sign of appearing.

Im Kkeokjeong also looked around anxiously.

“Yeah, why hasn’t it opened? Is the Gate broken?”

“…….”

What a horrifying thing to say.

As if Login Murim wasn’t enough, now there was Login Gate? If that was what this was, I’d rather bite my tongue and die.

Just as an ominous feeling began creeping over me, Butler Kim spoke.

“It appears the boss monster is still alive.”

“Alive? The boss monster?”

I pointed at Carus’s corpse, which lay facedown in a pool of blood, but Butler Kim shook his head.

“Named Monsters and boss monsters are different. To put it simply…the former is an uninvited guest, while the latter is the original homeowner.”

“The homeowner?”

“Yes. This may be easier to understand. If an armed intruder broke into your home, Hunter Jin Taekyung, what would you do?”

“I’d beat him until he begged me to kill him.”

“……I forgot. I meant if you were an ordinary person.”

“Oh. Then I’d run. If I thought I’d die before I could escape, I’d fight back.”

“The boss monster was no different. A powerful foe it could never hope to defeat appeared, so it fled in fear.”

The inside of a Gate was ultimately a world ruled by the law of the jungle.

The strong reigned, and the weak were trampled.

It might have been different for monsters that lived in tribes, but Wyverns were known to be solitary and ferocious. Carus wouldn’t have stopped after giving the boss monster a few knocks on the head and evicting it.

From the boss monster’s perspective, running away had been a fairly wise decision.

*Unfortunately, that just made things more troublesome for us.*

There was no way the thing had fled for its life only to hang around nearby grooming its claws.

It would have hidden as far away and as secretly as possible. And with only five people, searching this vast wasteland was impossible.

“Then…”

“We’ll have to go back to the entrance we came through.”

It was the obvious conclusion, and the right person for the job had already been decided.

Without giving it much thought, I shot my hand into the air.

“I’ll go.”

Team Leader Choi asked with concern in his eyes.

“You, Mr. Jin?”

“That seems like the fastest option. Doesn’t it?”

“That’s true, but you must be exhausted after the battle.”

*I just leveled up, damn it. Let me go.*

I swallowed the words that had risen to my throat and answered instead.

“I’m still full of energy. If you’re worried, I can have someone cast healing magic on me before I leave.”

“As you know, it’s a considerable distance to the entrance.”

“As you know, I’m pretty fast.”

It had taken us quite a while to reach this place the first time, but it would be different if I went alone. I wouldn’t have to stay on guard against monsters or match the pace of a group.

If I ran at full speed, I could reach the Gate entrance within an hour or two.

“Hmm. In that case, I’ll leave it to you. You and Butler Kim can go together.”

“Butler Kim, too?”

Butler Kim stroked his impressively full beard as he answered.

“We need to bring in outside personnel.”

Processing the byproducts of a Named Monster required Hunters who were at least B-Rank, if not A-Rank.

“I know a few people. If I go personally, they’ll probably drop everything and come running.”

“…….”

That sounded about right.

I still couldn’t forget the sight of the Sangdong Guild Master doing PT exercises[^3] while loudly repeating orders.

*It was something I could hardly believe even after seeing it.*

Knowing Butler Kim’s spectacular track record, I could only nod. We needed him if we wanted to bring in outside personnel.

“So it’ll just be Butler Kim and me?”

“Yes.”

Butler Kim nodded and stepped behind me.

“All right. I’m ready.”

“Pardon?”

“Would you bend over a little?”

“……Why do you need me to bend over?”

No, what exactly was he ready for? Why did I need to bend over?

A terrible suspicion crossed my mind.

“You don’t mean…soap?”

“Please carry me on your back.”

“Oh. Sure.”

Thank goodness. He wasn’t a centaur.

I let out a sigh of relief and willingly offered my back to Butler Kim.

* * *

Thud-thud-thud-thud-thud!

With Butler Kim on my back, I raced forward without slowing down.

We ran into a pack of Orcs wandering through the wasteland, but that was the only interruption.

“Fire Rain.”

The magic of an A-Rank mage.

One-third of the Orcs died beneath the downpour of fire, and the rest scattered in every direction.

I felt like a mobile turret.

*This isn’t bad.*

Just as I was thinking about how much more efficient raids would be if I did them this way, we crossed the barren wasteland and spotted a dense jungle ahead.

“You’re astonishingly fast. We’ve already reached the jungle.”

“I’m going to slow down from here. With all this vegetation, we could get lost.”

“I’ll follow your lead, Hunter Jin Taekyung.”

The jungle was nothing but trees and undergrowth, making it a maze where one could easily lose their way.

We slowed down and continued along our bearings.

That was when it happened.

“……Huh.”

I suddenly stopped, letting out a hollow laugh.

Puzzled by my abrupt halt, Butler Kim asked,

“What is it?”

“It’s nothing. Just…”

How was I supposed to explain this?

At last, I found the right word and added softly,

“There are hyenas.”

“Hyenas?”

“Yes.”

Stupid, persistent hyenas that kept baring their teeth even after I had let them go once.

I crooked my finger toward the dense undergrowth in the distance.

“Come out, you fucking bastards.”

Rustle.

The undergrowth shook, and the hyenas emerged one by one.

But my eyes were fixed on only one person.

> **System**
>
> **Lv. 80 Won Myunghoon**

“Would you look at this insolent bastard.”

The leader of the hyenas bared his teeth and growled.
